newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market rate eases back to 11.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market rate eases back to 11.1 pct.

text.p: Croatia's average money market rate eased back to 11.1 percent on Thursday from 11.6 percent, weighed down by a larger volume of call money loans at steady 10.5 percent.
Daily trade was put at 47.4 million, against 63 million in supply. Almost all of the 36.6 million kuna in fresh loans were call money, dealers said.
One bank accepted a lower price of 12 percent for a smaller two-week deal, down from 13 percent on Wednesday.
One three-week loan was struck at 14 percent, unchanged from a previous level.
Insurers rolled over old one-week loans at an unchanged 9.0 percent. Banks charged between 13 and 18 percent for renewed term deals.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Friday firmer at 6.0093 to the dollar and slightly weaker at 3.5757 against the German mark.
